title: Non-deterministic attention failure in quantized RLHF models — post-incident corrective measures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a mixed-precision rollout of an int8-enabled converter for RLHF-style chat models, we observed intermittent non-deterministic failures in the attention op within the quantized runtime. Symptoms included divergence in model output (accuracy drift), sporadic OOMs on warmed hosts, and a small number of crash loops that only manifested under multi-request batching. Impact: ~68% of canary traffic experienced degraded outputs for 3 hours, 12 customer jobs experienced reruns, and two enterprise customers opened support cases citing quality regressions. Root cause (hypothesis validated by reproducer): a race between KV-cache population and fused attention kernel path selection under the quantized codepath. Under certain sequence-length distributions and batching windows, the kernel selector chose a quantized fused-attention implementation that assumed a fully-populated KV cache; concurrent prefetched KV fragments produced partially-initialized buffers leading to NaN propagation and non-deterministic outputs. Compounding factor: insufficient telemetry for fractional KV population states and lack of deterministic canary coverage for mixed-batch sequence-length distributions. Scope: Hosts running runtime-1.23 with int8-converter enabled on nvidia-A100-80GB dedicated pools. Corrective goals: 1) Eliminate race in kernel selection or make kernel selection conservative when KV state is not-known-good; 2) Improve telemetry to catch fractional KV population and kernel mismatch; 3) Add deterministic canary tests for mixed sequence-length batching; 4) Provide an immediate mitigation to prevent customer-facing regressions until a stable runtime patch ships.

root_cause_analysis: The quantized runtime's kernel selection logic assumed that KV cache population is atomic relative to kernel path decision. In the mixed-batch, multi-request continuous batching scenario, the attention kernel selector executed concurrently with KV writes (prefetch and partial copies). A codepath in the int8 fused-attention kernel lacked guards against partially-zeroed or partially-filled KV buffers. Because quantized kernels perform aggressive in-place transformations, partially-initialized inputs could produce NaNs that propagated through subsequent fused ops. Tests that previously validated the converter used single-request deterministic traces and missed this interleaving. Additionally, our telemetry did not emit a 'kv_population_fraction' metric and our canary test harness did not model high variance sequence-length mixes common in RLHF prompts. The combination allowed the issue to slip past canary checks and hit wider canary traffic under a rollout spike.
short_term_mitigations: Disable int8 converter on affected allocators until stable runtime patch lands (completed 2025-08-12).
Hotfix: kernel selector now checks KV completeness flag before selecting fused-attention path; otherwise choose dequantized-safe attention (PR #7854).
Temporary runtime policy: if batch sequence-length stddev > 200 or kv_population_fraction < 0.95, route to dequantized attention path.
Customer comms: notified affected enterprise customers and opened support tickets with recommended workarounds (conversation thread links attached in comments).
long_term_action_items: A1: Add explicit 'kv_population_fraction' telemetry and an SLI that triggers when fraction < 0.99 on production hosts (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 5).
A2: Harden fused attention kernels with defensive checks and zero-safe fast paths; introduce unit tests that inject partially-initialized KV buffers (owner: Marco Li, estimate: 8).

A3: Expand canary harness to replay production trace mixes, including RLHF prompt sequence-length distributions and multi-request batching scenarios (owner: Ethan Morales, estimate: 8, due: 2025-09-10).
A4: Add an automated preflight that simulates batch variance before every converter rollout and gate rollouts if deviation > threshold (owner: SRE oncall team, estimate: 3).
A5: Improve converter release notes with explicit compatibility matrix for pooled autoscaling and known safe attention kernels per hardware SKU (owner: Docs, estimate: 2).
A6: Create a regression test in CI that runs stochastic interleaving tests across quantized kernels under constrained memory to catch OOM/crash loops (owner: CI infra, estimate: 5).
A7: Build a canary observability dashboard that correlates kernel selection, kv_population_fraction, sequence-length variance, and quality SLO deltas (owner: Console team, estimate: 3).
acceptance_criteria: All host telemetry emits 'kv_population_fraction' and it is visible on the observability dashboard.
Fused-attention kernel passes injected partial-KV unit tests under quantized and mixed-batch modes.
Canary harness replays production RLHF traces and shows no quality regression across 72-hour windows for runtime-1.24 with int8 enabled.
Rollback policy and preflight gate prevent converter rollouts when batch-variance thresholds are exceeded.
No customer-facing regressions related to attention or NaN propagation after full rollout for 7 days.
risks_and_open_questions: Risk: Tightening kernel guards may incur a 3-7% tail latency regression for long-sequence workloads—need perf acceptance tradeoff (performance owner: Rahul Singh).
Question: Should we prefer a conservative default (disable int8 fused-attention by default) until a full auditoried pass is complete? Decision deferred to PM and Runtime Tech Lead.
Risk: Canary trace replay may not fully capture live multi-tenant burst patterns; consider metallic load testing on dedicated staging pools.
Question: Which customers should be proactively offered extended dedicated capacity or alternative model variants during rollout? (CS to propose list).
